scope: Visual art direction of current published hero, discussion only; no site changes.

steps.health: Clear product recognition; competing typography and dominant packaging weaken hierarchy.
findings: Oversized product name repeats prominent pack name.
Heavy headline, brush script, vintage pack lettering and cartoon compete.
Very even orange breading and symmetrical cut suggest staged/rendered food.

steps.health: Readable and CTA visible; strong poster treatment crowds hierarchy.
findings: The wordmark/name/script dominate the upper screen.
Package and prepared-food cutouts remain separate objects rather than one photographic scene.
Background pocket balances the diagonal, so adding decoration is unlikely to solve the core issue.

steps.health: Brand palette and product catalogue are consistent; first product is repeated.
findings: Large hero package is immediately repeated as first catalogue item.
The first screen adds little occasion or atmosphere beyond product identification.

strengths: Prepared product and product action are clear.
recommendation: Test one edit of the concept: prepared food as the main focal point, package35–40% smaller, calmer heading and small handwritten annotation. Use natural food photography with one light direction. Keep Novoferma character and warm palette.
limits: Qualitative visual assessment from fresh browser captures, not conversion research or complete accessibility certification. CTA is visibly large; package print is too small to serve as required product information on mobile.
